pr.title: Show Pending when only an earlier head was reviewed
pr.head: 7584f800d9daaf4148ab0837e30760f5378e660b

summary: The Projector site shows a review status for each pull request: in a summary page's header, on the pull request's row on the Reviews index, and in the banner of a project that an open pull request proposes. Until a pull request is merged or closed, that status is the verdict of the newest Projector review of the head the page describes, Clean or Changes requested.

Each head has its own status, because the newest verdict wins and a verdict covers only the commit it reviewed. So when the site was built before a new head's review landed, that head read Unreviewed, even if earlier heads had been reviewed several times. A pull request that the reviewers had looked at read as one nobody had looked at.

This pull request adds a fourth status, pending. A head shows it when no Projector review names the head but an earlier head of the same pull request has a verdict. The status carries that newest earlier verdict as last, and the site draws a Pending chip that links that review and names it in its tooltip. Unreviewed now means no verdict on this head or on any earlier one.

cards.title: The four statuses
cards.html:
StatusWhen a head shows it
clean, changes-requestedA Projector review names this head. The newest such review decides, whichever model wrote it.
pendingNo review names this head, and an earlier head has a verdict. Links the newest earlier verdict.
unreviewedNo review names this head or any earlier head.

Merged and Closed replace all four once the pull request is merged or closed.

cards.title: What counts as an earlier head
cards.html:
The site knows when each summary was published, not when each head was pushed. So a head counts as earlier unless its summary is newer than the page's own summary. A reviewed head that the site has no summary of counts as earlier, because the site cannot place it in time.

An older head whose only reviewed heads are later stays Unreviewed: no review is coming for it.

groups.title: Choose each page's status
groups.kicker: The build decides which status each head's page shows.
intro: The site build asks GitHub for each pull request's reviews once. review_statuses turns them into each head's newest Projector verdict. The new head_status picks the status for one page from that table, so the code that reads and trusts verdicts stays in one place.

For head_status to find the newest verdict on an earlier head, the table needs an order. review_statuses now returns heads sorted by when their deciding review was submitted, oldest first, and head_status takes the last earlier entry.

files.note: Adds head_status, sorts review_statuses by review time, and passes each page the heads with newer summaries.

checks.text: versions and heads are both sorted newest first by summary_time, so heads[:i] holds exactly the heads whose summaries are newer than this page's. Replacing it with an empty set fails test_a_verdict_on_a_later_head_leaves_an_earlier_one_unreviewed.

at is GitHub's submittedAt timestamp, and pr_status drops reviews that have none, so the sort never compares a missing value. Dropping the sort fails test_a_head_only_earlier_heads_were_reviewed_on_is_pending_on_the_newest_of_them, because a dict keeps a head at its first insertion position.
A verdict on the head itself returns first, so it always wins over a newer verdict on an earlier head. An incremental verdict is a verdict like any other here.

files.note: Adds the pending variant to ReviewStatus, with the verdict, head, and URL of the newest earlier review as last.

groups.title: Draw the Pending chip
groups.kicker: One shared function draws the status everywhere the site shows it.
intro: statusHtml draws the status for the summary header, the Reviews row, and a proposed project's banner. A pending status becomes a link to the last review, with a title such as "Last review: changes requested on e333044. This head hasn't been reviewed yet." The chip is a link, so a keyboard reaches it and a screen reader reads the title.
The chip has its own slate colour, --pending, in the light palette and in both dark palettes: the one the reader's system asks for and the one the reader picks.

files.note: Adds the Pending branch to statusHtml and a verdictWord helper that the chip and its tooltip share.

checks.text: Both href and title pass through esc, which escapes ". Merged and Closed return before this branch, so they still take the chip's place.

files.note: Adds the --pending token to the three palettes and the .rstatus.pending rule.

intro: docs/cli.md describes the Pending chip where it describes a summary's header. The tests cover the build's choice of status and the chip's rendering, which runs through node.
